documents.abstract: This paper proposes a Kriging-based metamodel for real-time taxiing time prediction on complex airport surface networks. By combining the strengths of analytical and machine learning methods, the model offers superior adaptability and interpretability. It produces not only accurate point predictions but also confidence intervals to quantify predictive uncertainty, with each prediction traceable to specific training samples. The model relies on simple and readily available inputs, including flight schedules and observed runway-queue information, which facilitates adaptation to other airports after local calibration. Trained on historical operational records and evaluated through high-fidelity simulations of Beijing Capital International Airport and benchmarked against current operational methods and artificial intelligence-based alternatives, the results demonstrate significant improvements over existing taxi-time estimation techniques. These advantages highlight the model’s potential as a robust solution for future automated air traffic management systems.

Most artificial intelligence models for electrocardiogram (ECG) interpretation rely on task-specific supervised learning, requiring dedicated labeled datasets for each diagnostic task and limiting scalability across diverse cardiac conditions. This study investigated whether vision-language learning from paired ECG recordings and summary reports could enable transferable ECG representations without task-specific supervised training. We developed ECG-VLM, a contrastive vision-language model consisting of a Transformer-based image encoder and a text encoder, trained on 800,034 paired 10-s ECG recordings and summary reports from the MIMIC-IV-ECG database. Cardiac condition detection was performed using natural-language prompts without condition-specific retraining or fine-tuning. Performance was evaluated on an internal test set and externally validated using the LSAS-ECG dataset (45,151 recordings) across 14 cardiac conditions, together with retrieval and subgroup analysis. ECG-VLM achieved diagnostic performance across 14 cardiac conditions, with AUROC ranging from 0.679 to 0.981 on the internal test set and from 0.691 to 0.991 on external validation. Performance was strongest for rhythm abnormalities (mean AUROC 0.948 internally and 0.921 externally) and lower for morphological conditions. Compared with the previously reported signal-based ECG-CLIP framework, ECG-VLM achieved comparable performance for rhythm abnormalities while improving AUPRC for several morphological conditions. Performance remained broadly consistent across external validation and demographic and clinical subgroups. These findings demonstrate the feasibility of vision-language supervision from paired ECG recordings and summary reports for learning transferable ECG representations without task-specific supervised training. This framework provides a basis for future extension of vision-language learning to ECG images encountered in routine clinical practice.

Abstract A persistent gap separates academic research priorities from the operational challenges faced by manufacturing firms. Established identification methods, among them Failure Mode and Effects Analysis (FMEA) workshops, Lean audits and consultant engagements, are episodic, bounded by participant expertise and organised along departmental lines, which makes cross-departmental issues hard to surface. Multi-agent systems built on large language models (LLMs) have meanwhile shown collaborative problem-solving ability in software engineering and, more recently, in shopfloor scheduling and supply chain coordination. This article is a Perspective. It develops a framework and a research agenda; implementation and empirical evaluation fall outside its scope and are set out as its first research priorities. Three contributions are offered. The first is a synthesis of literature from industrial problem identification, LLM-based autonomous agents and manufacturing AI, which positions the proposal against existing industrial LLM agent work. The second is a framework in which six domain-specialised agents (production, quality, maintenance, supply chain, safety, energy) would collaborate through a five-phase protocol: worker-driven discovery, cross-departmental analysis, candidate-relationship detection, consensus-based financial assessment and debate-driven prioritisation. The prioritisation procedure is fully specified, including the normalisation of financial estimates, a measure of estimate dispersion, the derivation of criteria weights, a non-compensatory gate for safety-critical items and a mandatory human verification step. The third is a worked calculation on a hypothetical steel manufacturing vignette, included so that the procedure can be reproduced and scrutinised rather than as evidence of effectiveness. A preliminary qualitative readiness assessment and a three-horizon agenda of fourteen research questions complete the paper. The benefits identified are presented as hypotheses for that agenda to test rather than as demonstrated outcomes.

documents.abstract: Pediatric speech and language assessment supports the early identification of communication difficulties and access to timely intervention. Large language models (LLMs) and related generative artificial intelligence technologies are increasingly being incorporated into systems that analyze children’s speech and language data. However, evidence regarding their application in pediatric assessment remains limited and fragmented. This scoping review aimed to map and critically examine research on LLM-enabled systems used to assess children’s speech, language, and communication abilities. Four databases were searched, and seven studies met the inclusion criteria. Data were charted according to study design, purpose, participant and target-population characteristics, assessment domain, type of LLM, model input, role of the LLM, additional artificial-intelligence components, evaluation methods, and reported outcomes. The findings provide preliminary evidence of technical feasibility and agreement with human or reference-based assessments. However, the evidence remains limited because of small or restricted datasets, the use of synthetic data in some cases, limited real-world validation, and concerns regarding fairness and generalizability across languages and clinical populations. Further research is necessary to establish clinical validity, reliability, and appropriate use of LLM-enabled systems before their broader implementation in pediatric speech and language assessment.

documents.abstract: Rationale of Study: This study reviews common analytical techniques for decision-making, analyses their applications and effectiveness, and identifies the required skills. It also explores contextual factors like interpretability, data quality, and skill gaps that hinder implementation, offering insights for practitioners and researchers. Methodology: This study reviews 27 peer-reviewed articles from 2019-2024, using PRISMA to map analytical techniques for decision-making. It shows a shift from descriptive to predictive and prescriptive analytics, mainly driven by ML and AI. The research also suggests combining automated systems with human judgment to enhance decision-making amid complex, data-rich environments. Findings: The study highlights a shift from descriptive to predictive and prescriptive analytics, driven by advances in machine learning (ML) and artificial intelligence (AI). To build trust and adoption, strong data governance, ongoing professional development, and clear AI model explanations are crucial. Future research should balance interpretability with real-time analytics and integrate automated systems with human judgment to enhance performance. Implications: Access to this information fosters a culture of informed decision-making. Developing data governance is vital to ensure data quality, integrity, and ethical use. Qualified professionals with industry knowledge and technical skills are in short supply. Integrating data scientists, analysts, and decision-makers requires expertise in statistics, programming, data storytelling, and strategy. The paper recommends investing in the professional growth of cross-functional analytics teams. Originality: The rapid adoption of machine learning and AI has shifted decision-making from descriptive reporting to predictive and prescriptive approaches. Extracting insights from complex datasets is now a key competitive edge.

Reliable evaluation of artificial intelligence models for coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) imaging remains challenging because patient-level dependencies, source-related biases, and differences between imaging modalities can lead to overly optimistic performance estimates. This study proposes a leakage-controlled, modality-aware deep ensemble framework for COVID-19 classification using chest X-ray (CXR) and computed tomography (CT) images from the COVID-19 Radiography Database and the SARS-CoV-2 CT-Scan Dataset. Separate evaluation protocols were established for CXR and CT, with duplicate control and available source information incorporated for CXR and patient-level partitioning applied to CT before data augmentation. Four ImageNet-pretrained convolutional neural networks (CNNs)—VGG16, ResNet50, DenseNet169, and InceptionV3—were evaluated, followed by temperature scaling for probability calibration and validation-optimized weighted soft voting for ensemble fusion. The original CT architectural comparison was conducted at the slice level, whereas the final CT evaluation was performed at the patient level. In the final modality-specific held-out evaluation, DenseNet169 achieved an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC) of 0.985, an accuracy of 97.32%, and an F1-score of 98.1% on the 2870-image CXR test set. The calibrated weighted ensemble achieved an AUROC of 0.990, an accuracy of 98.43%, and an F1-score of 97.9%, with a Brier score of 0.030 and an expected calibration error (ECE) of 0.023. For CT, DenseNet169 achieved an AUROC of 0.941 and correctly classified 16 of 18 patients (88.89%), whereas the calibrated weighted ensemble achieved an AUROC of 0.969 and correctly classified 17 of 18 patients (94.44%), with a Brier score of 0.070 and an ECE of 0.053. An uncertainty-aware selective-prediction analysis identified 316 of 2870 CXR test images (11.01%) and 2 of 18 CT test patients (11.11%) as low-confidence cases for specialist review. Among the remaining CT cases, 15 of 16 patients were correctly classified (93.75%). Because the CT test cohort contained only 18 patients, the patient-level CT performance and selective-prediction results should be interpreted cautiously as descriptive estimates from this limited cohort. The original pooled evaluation, in which DenseNet169 achieved 98.51% accuracy, is retained only as an exploratory architectural comparison and should not be interpreted as directly comparable with the final modality-specific evaluation. The findings demonstrate that evaluation design, statistical unit, probability calibration, and ensemble fusion materially influence the interpretation of COVID-19 imaging-classification performance. The proposed framework provides leakage-aware and calibrated performance estimates under the evaluated datasets; however, independent multicenter external validation is required before broader claims of clinical generalizability or deployment readiness can be made.

documents.abstract: This chapter brings John Dewey’s account of educative experience into conversation with Meighan’s sociological analysis of control and agency in schooling, and Zimmerman’s model of self-regulated learning, to clarify what it means to “learn how to learn” across the life course. It argues that learning to learn is neither a generic skill nor an individual trait, but a set of capacities cultivated through intentionally designed experiences, clear expectations, and structured opportunities for reflection, uptake of feedback, and purposeful action. Learner agency is shaped not only by formal institutional arrangements but also by tacit classroom norms, peer dynamics, and the emotional conditions required for risk-taking and self-monitoring. This chapter also considers contemporary pressures, especially the ease of fluent artificial intelligence (AI)-generated answers that can short-circuit reflective effort unless learners are explicitly guided to plan, monitor, and evaluate their thinking. Through an integrative framework and a practical evidence map, including marginalia from practising teachers, the chapter illustrates how these ideas travel into classroom judgement. It offers design principles for educators who wish to build autonomy without abandoning structure and to support diverse learners in developing sustainable habits of inquiry, critique, and lifelong learning (LLL). It serves as a conceptual runway in teacher education and related modules.

Complete illustrated English and French editions of Learning to Welcome the Answer / Apprendre à accueillir la réponse, a research essay by Jean-Sébastien Beaulieu. English abstract I examine what it means to welcome a mathematical answer produced with artificial intelligence while preserving the understanding that makes an answer useful. The article begins with my response to OpenAI's release of mathematical manuscripts and the perspective acquired through four years of work on my own project. Thirty sources guide an exploration of proof, formalization, computation, fractal geometry, classification, research provenance and digital protection. Each technical example connects a concept with its assumptions and the conditions of a possible application. The discussion then turns toward Book III with Aguilar and my preparation for NASA Space Apps. A geometric descriptor offers a concrete research question: what information would it contribute under a fair comparison? Feature addition and adaptive selection of an analysis scale remain distinct experimental proposals. Their assessment calls for defined observables, appropriate reference methods, an availability record for the data and reproducible evaluation. I place these questions within a wider concern for participation. Clear explanations, usable research materials and accessible tools help people turn curiosity into sustained work. My position is an invitation to celebrate shared knowledge through careful reading, explicit validation and practical contribution. The work invested in a question becomes part of the judgment with which a new answer is received. Résumé français J'examine ce que signifie accueillir une réponse mathématique produite avec l'intelligence artificielle tout en préservant la compréhension qui la rend utile. L'article part de ma réaction à la publication de manuscrits mathématiques par OpenAI et du regard acquis au cours de quatre années consacrées à mon propre projet. Trente sources accompagnent une exploration de la preuve, de la formalisation, du calcul, de la géométrie fractale, de la classification, de la provenance des travaux et de la protection numérique. Chaque exemple technique relie un concept à ses hypothèses et aux conditions d'une application possible. La réflexion se poursuit vers le Livre III avec Aguilar et ma préparation à NASA Space Apps. Un descripteur géométrique fournit une question de recherche concrète : quelle information apporterait-il dans une comparaison équitable ? L'ajout d'une variable et le choix adaptatif d'une échelle d'analyse demeurent deux propositions expérimentales distinctes. Leur évaluation appelle des observables définies, des méthodes de référence adaptées, un registre de disponibilité des données et un protocole reproductible. J'inscris ces questions dans une préoccupation plus large pour la participation. Des explications claires, des ressources de recherche utilisables et des outils accessibles aident à transformer la curiosité en travail durable. Ma position invite à célébrer le partage des connaissances par une lecture attentive, une validation explicite et une contribution concrète. Le travail investi dans une question nourrit le jugement avec lequel une réponse nouvelle est accueillie. Each edition includes the introduction, nine chapters, conclusion, 27-term glossary, 30 references, three infographics, and front and back covers. Reported mathematical claims retain their stated verification scope; prospective applications remain research questions.

The increasing availability of artificial intelligence (AI) tools presents new opportunities and challenges for teaching and learning in higher education. This study examined lecturers’ awareness of and attitudes towards the use of AI tools at the University of Nigeria, Nsukka. A descriptive survey design was adopted. Four research questions and two hypotheses guided the study. The population comprised academic staff in the Department of Science Education, University of Nigeria, Nsukka, from whom 49 lecturers participated in the study. Data were collected using a researcher-developed instrument titled Questionnaire on Lecturers’ Awareness Level and Attitude to AI Tools (QLALAAIT). The instrument was subjected to face validation and trial testing, and its overall reliability coefficient, determined using Cronbach’s alpha, was 0.83. Data were analysed using mean and standard deviation to answer the research questions, while analysis of variance (ANOVA) was used to test the hypotheses at the 0.05 level of significance. The findings indicated that lecturers demonstrated awareness of selected AI tools, including ChatGPT, Turnitin, and QuillBot, and generally expressed positive attitudes towards their use in educational contexts. Further analysis showed that years of teaching experience did not significantly influence lecturers’ awareness of or attitudes towards AI tools. The study highlights the need for structured professional development, institutional support, and access to appropriate resources to facilitate informed and effective use of AI tools in university teaching and related academic activities.

documents.abstract: Artificial intelligence is the challenge of the new era that has imposed its presence and intervened in various aspects of life, especially the science of law. Will the machine improve the art of drafting legal texts to control human behavior, now that its intelligence has surpassed that of humans? Have legal texts addressed such dangerous interference that has included several fields, starting from copyright and e-commerce to the point of the existence of predictive judiciary as an alternative to traditional judiciary governed by machines? Is the law really going through the digitization crisis imposed on it by reality? We are facing a new challenge, and a new legal arsenal is required to regulate its provisions and benefit from its advantages.

The transformation of higher education has increased the need to articulate classroom-based innovation with institutional management and governance processes. In this context, academics who assume academic program leadership responsibilities occupy an intermediate position between teaching practice and strategic management, although the literature frequently addresses these dimensions separately. This article aims to analyze and integrate recent literature on academic leadership, pedagogical innovation, governance, and faculty development in higher education, with particular attention to the role of academic middle leaders as agents connecting educational practice and institutional change. An integrative literature review was conducted based on thematic relevance, recency, scientific quality, and availability of DOI, complemented by regional evidence concerning artificial intelligence adoption and governance in Latin American and Caribbean higher education. The thematic synthesis identified four interconnected dimensions: adaptive and innovative leadership, academic middle leadership, shared governance, and servant leadership. The findings suggest that institutionalizing innovation depends not only on individual faculty initiative but also on organizational conditions that promote participation, trust, capacity development, and shared decision-making. The study concludes that academic program leaders who maintain a teaching role can become strategic actors connecting pedagogical innovation with institutional management when they have adequate autonomy, leadership development, and organizational support.

The 2D Crystal Consortium Materials Innovation Platform (2DCC-MIP) is a NSF supported national user facility focused on advancing the synthesis of 2D materials, monolayers, surfaces, and interfaces. The need for the facility to organize and share data with users led to the development of an internal data management and analysis engine, the Lifetime Sample Tracking platform (LiST). This infrastructure allows the automated capture, curation, analysis, and dissemination of data ranging from experimental materials synthesis parameters and characterization to theoretical first-principles and ReaxFF molecular dynamics modeling [Nayir et al., 2D Mater. 10, 032002 (2023)]. The system currently hosts synthesis and property data (accessible via a REST API) on ∼20 000 samples produced by the 2DCC grown using a variety of techniques from bulk crystal growth to metal-organic chemical vapor deposition and molecular beam epitaxy, among others. Data used in publications can easily be grouped by the system into data packages that are given digital object identifiers for inclusion with each publication. The LiST platform is now being used by groups outside of the 2DCC as a solution for data curation in materials science. Data management tools, such as LiST, support the materials development process by allowing a closed loop iteration between synthesis, characterization, theory, and targeted materials design. This also enables machine learning research, artificial intelligence analysis, and the potential for autonomous synthesis in the future.

The next generation of particle physics experiments will face an era of challenges in data acquisition, due to unprecedented data rates and volumes along with extreme environments and operational constraints. Harnessing these data for scientific discovery demands real-time inference and decision-making, intelligent data reduction, and efficient processing architectures beyond current capabilities. Crucial to the success of this experimental paradigm are several emerging technologies, such as artificial intelligence and machine learning, silicon microelectronics, and the advent of quantum algorithms and processing. Their intersection includes areas of research such as low-power and low-latency devices for edge computing, heterogeneous accelerator systems, reconfigurable hardware, codesign and synthesis strategies, readout for cryogenic or high-radiation environments, and analog computing. This white paper presents a community-driven vision to identify and prioritize research and development opportunities in hardware-based ML systems and corresponding physics applications, contributing toward a successful transition to the data frontier of fundamental science.

The rapid adoption of generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) in advertising since 2022 has transformed content production while raising concerns about the preservation of brand authenticity, a critical foundation of consumer trust and brand relationships. This study examines how AI-generated advertising influences perceived brand authenticity, identifies the mechanisms driving authenticity erosion, and explains the contextual factors that account for inconsistent findings in prior research. Following PRISMA 2020 guidelines, this review synthesizes 13 studies published between 2022 and 2026 retrieved from the Web of Science Core Collection and EBSCOhost databases. Through thematic synthesis, this study identifies three interrelated mechanisms through which AI-generated advertising may undermine brand authenticity: disclosure effects, failed anthropomorphism, and sincerity erosion. The findings further reveal that the effects of AI-generated advertising on authenticity perceptions are contingent upon individual characteristics, product and brand contexts, and source-related factors, including AI capability beliefs, product type, luxury positioning, and communicator characteristics. This study develops an integrated framework explaining when and why AI-generated advertising enhances or undermines brand authenticity, thus providing theoretical insights for consumer research and practical implications for AI-enabled marketing decision-making.
topics: Consumer Behavior in Brand Consumption and Identification

documents.abstract: Agricultural work remains physically demanding and strongly seasonal in many production systems, while labour scarcity, rising wages, ageing farm populations, and competing non-farm employment are increasing pressure to complete operations with less human effort. This critical narrative review evaluates how mechanization and agronomic redesign can reduce farm drudgery and labour requirement without assuming that labour saved at an individual task is equivalent to labour displaced from agriculture. Literature published from 1 January 1990 to 6 August 2026 was identified through accessible scholarly databases and indexes, supplemented by citation searching and authoritative institutional sources. Evidence was appraised for study design, measurement of labour and ergonomic outcomes, external validity, treatment of confounding, duration, and attention to gender, safety, and implementation conditions. The strongest evidence indicates that mechanization can markedly reduce time and physiological burden in power-intensive and repetitive operations, but whole-farm labour effects vary because mechanization also changes cultivated area, input intensity, timeliness, and the allocation of family and hired labour. Ergonomic hand tools and scale-appropriate machines are especially important where capital-intensive mechanization is infeasible. Agronomic approaches such as zero or reduced tillage and direct-seeded rice can remove labour-intensive operations, yet their labour-saving value is conditional on weed control, crop establishment, residue management, and access to compatible equipment. Conservation agriculture illustrates this conditionality: manual planting basins or increased hand weeding can offset labour savings, whereas mechanized establishment and effective weed management can reduce peak labour demand. Gendered task allocation, machinery access, custom hiring services, occupational safety, and rural employment transitions determine who benefits and who bears adjustment costs. Robotics and autonomous equipment may address labour shortages in selected systems, but economic feasibility, field reliability, supervision, and human-machine safety remain important constraints. The review concludes that drudgery reduction is best pursued through integrated mechanization-agronomy packages evaluated with task-specific ergonomic measures and whole-household, whole-season labour accounting.

This article is devoted to a comprehensive study of media neophraseologisms as relevant markers of transformation processes in the modern Russian phraseological system. Using extensive empirical data from the Russian-language online press and Telegram channels for 2020–2026, the article identifies key derivational trends in neophraseology: structural diffuseness, pragmemization, and sententialization of signs. We demonstrate a semantic shift in neoidioms toward de-abstraction and connection to the current agenda and substantiate the adaptive nature of phraseological innovations in the context of an increasingly complex information picture of the world. Particular attention is paid to the anthropocentric aspect of linguistic creativity: The generation of neophraseologisms, mediated by the mechanisms of irony, allusion, and manipulation, is verified as a demarcation line between the natural human text generation and the algorithms of generative artificial intelligence. We propose a typology of neophraseologisms, including discursive-precedent, intermedia, and calqued units, including their axiological and ludic functions in media texts. The article notes that the diffuseness of structure and pragmemization act as mechanisms of linguistic economy, while the de-abstraction of signs reflects the connection between phraseology and extralinguistic factors. The results are significant for lexicographic practice, university teaching, and media stylistics. The developed typology and the identified derivational processes can serve as a basis for monitoring the Russian phraseological system evolution. The results of the study are applicable in lexicographic practice, teaching, and media stylistics.

Musculoskeletal disorders (MSDs) are conditions affecting the muscles, bones, joints, tendons, ligaments, cartilage, and other supporting structures of the body. They may be acute or chronic and can result from trauma, repetitive movements, poor posture, aging, genetic factors, occupational hazards, or inflammatory diseases. Common musculoskeletal disorders include osteoarthritis, rheumatoid arthritis, osteoporosis, low back pain, tendinitis, bursitis, fractures, and muscle strains.The main symptoms are pain, swelling, stiffness, muscle weakness, restricted joint movements, and difficulty performing daily activities. Diagnosis is based on medical history, physical examination, and investigations such as X-rays, CT scans, MRI, blood tests, and bone mineral density measurements, depending on the condition.Treatment aims to relieve pain, reduce inflammation, restore mobility, and prevent disability. Management includes medications, physiotherapy, therapeutic exercises, heat and cold therapy, occupational therapy, and lifestyle modifications. In severe cases, surgical intervention may be necessary. Medical rehabilitation plays an essential role in improving muscle strength, joint flexibility, balance, coordination, and functional independence.Prevention involves maintaining correct posture, regular physical activity, a balanced diet rich in calcium and vitamin D, maintaining a healthy body weight, using proper workplace ergonomics, and avoiding repetitive strain. Early diagnosis and appropriate treatment help reduce complications and improve quality of life. A multidisciplinary approach involving doctors, physiotherapists, and occupational therapists is essential for effective management and long-term recovery.

topics: Ethics and Social Impacts of AI

documents.abstract: Digital technology has evolved rapidly, resulting in a new form of marketing known as "meta marketing," which represents a revolutionary way of doing business in today's rapidly changing marketplace, especially for marketers working within the highly competitive Fast-Moving Consumer Goods (FMCG) industry.This study aimed to conceptually explore how organizations utilize technology such as the Metaverse, augmented reality (AR), virtual reality (VR), and artificial intelligence (AI) to create meta marketing strategies, while promoting sustainable development.This will include investigating how using immersive, interactive marketing environments can motivate consumer engagement, trust, and purchasing behaviours, while at the same time, through lessening physical consumption of resources and improving digital communications, developing initiatives that encompass environmental sustainability.Using existing literature and applying theoretical frameworks, this research advances knowledge by developing a conceptual framework that connects the advancement of technological innovation with achieving sustainable outcomes as a business performance indicator.Overall, this study provides evidence that the use of Meta marketing presents FMCG companies with an opportunity to gain a competitive advantage while meeting sustainability challenges.

The Boolean Satisfiability Problem is a central challenge in artificial intelligence and combinatorial optimization, with applications in circuit verification, planning, and bioinformatics. This study makes two main contributions: a systematic review of metaheuristic approaches conducted under the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) protocol, and a comparative evaluation of 11 algorithms. The considered methods include genetic algorithms, genetic algorithms with stepwise adaptation of weights, hybrid grey wolf genetic algorithms, genetic-based local search, population-based simulated annealing, dynamic clause weighting local search, stochastic local search, phase transition-based local search, random walk with local (1 + 1) evolutionary algorithm, improved adaptive genetic algorithm, and artificial bee colony. The evaluation relies on multiple criteria, including solution quality, robustness, success rate with confidence intervals, computational efficiency, and scalability across the benchmark families UF20 to UF250, complemented by additional benchmarks from the SAT Challenge Random Track (2018) and newly generated random 3-SAT instances. The results show that Genetic Algorithm, phase transition-based local search, dynamic clause weighting local search, genetic-based local search, random walk with local (1+1) Evolutionary Algorithm, and Artificial Bee Colony provide the most robust performance, maintaining a balance between exploration and exploitation. Beyond comparisons within metaheuristics, the study also examines how bio-inspired approaches compare with modern SAT solvers based on conflict-driven clause learning and stochastic local search across different problem scales. By contrast, highly specialized variants, such as genetic algorithms with stepwise adaptation of weights, population-based simulated annealing, hybrid grey wolf genetic algorithms, and improved adaptive genetic algorithms, degrade significantly on larger benchmarks. Overall, this study consolidates the strengths and weaknesses of metaheuristics and outlines future directions for adaptability, hybridization with machine learning, and scalable computations.

The article analyzes the penetration of artificial intelligence (AI) tools into programming education, their didactic opportunities and risks. A four-component methodological model is proposed for using AI tools while preserving students' independent programming skills and algorithmic thinking: staged use of AI, developing AI-collaboration competence, renewing the assessment system, and project-based learning. The model can be applied in teaching programming and computer science at higher education institutions.

The rapid development of artificial intelligence (AI) technologies and computer networks has triggered the sudden leap in the world energy requirements and heightened the stress on the idea of environmental sustainability. The renewable energy sources, such as solar, wind and hydro sources, are very attractive alternatives to fossil fuels but due to their intermittency nature, there are serious issues related to the forecasting accuracy, energy storage and grid stability. The chapter is a survey of various methodological strategies in optimizing renewable energy systems that are based on data-centric, AI-based tools that include machine-learning models, digital-twin systems, metaheuristic optimization algorithms, and lifecycle assessment models. These methods of computation increase the level of energy forecasting, simplify the real-time monitoring of the working system, optimize energy distribution, and manage storage resources.

Microfluidics has emerged as an important platform for manipulating and analyzing small volumes of fluids, cells, biomolecules, and particles with high precision. Its ability to control microscale flows and integrate multiple analytical steps has enabled diverse biomedical technologies, including lab-on-a-chip, point-of-care diagnostics, organ-on-chip, and microphysiological systems. This review summarizes the fundamental principles of biomedical microfluidics, including microscale fluid dynamics, laminar flow, diffusion, and key dimensionless parameters, together with major platform formats such as continuous-flow, droplet-based, and digital microfluidics. Recent fabrication approaches, including photolithography, soft lithography, molding, laser-based methods, 3D printing, micromilling, and paper- and lamination-based techniques, are also discussed. The review highlights applications in cancer and liquid biopsy, infectious disease diagnostics, cardiovascular and neurological disorders, organ-on-chip models, drug screening and toxicity testing, pharmaceutical synthesis, drug delivery, single-cell analysis, and regenerative and reproductive medicine. Particular attention is given to the growing use of microfluidics for personalized and human-relevant biomedical research. The review further examines the major challenges associated with microfluidic biomedical systems, including fabrication reproducibility, material compatibility, biological complexity, standardization, scalability and manufacturing, clinical validation, regulatory requirements, and integration with advanced computational approaches such as artificial intelligence and machine learning. Finally, future perspectives are discussed, with particular emphasis on personalized medicine, decentralized diagnostics, human-relevant drug development, multi-organ microphysiological systems, wearable and implantable microfluidics, and automated biomedical platforms.
topics: Innovative Microfluidic and Catalytic Techniques Innovation

documents.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly embedded in research software, yet many integrations preserve only the visible prompt and answer while losing structured evidence about configuration, provider metadata, timing, failures, and the exact request procedure. MiND is an open-source, provider-neutral middleware that places a small audit boundary between an application and an LLM. For each attempted interaction it normalizes the input, constructs an explicit request, invokes a provider adapter, normalizes the result, and stores a versioned Cycle Artifact containing the observable execution context. The same core is available through a Python API, command-line interface, local HTTP API, and a self-contained Windows interface. MiND is deliberately non-agentic: it does not infer human intention, expose hidden model reasoning, or claim deterministic repetition of stochastic model output. Its purpose is narrower—to make the surrounding execution procedure inspectable and reusable.

Abstract The translation of deep learning architectures from controlled experimental settings into real-world cancer diagnostics is heavily bottlenecked by domain shift and demographic bias. While models routinely achieve near-perfect retrospective performance on internal datasets, validation across external multicenter cohorts incurs a systemic and severe performance degradation, with an average metric drop of 0.16 AUC. This review provides a comprehensive metasynthesis of contemporary algorithmic mitigation paradigms designed to alleviate distribution discrepancies, evaluating techniques ranging from classical stain normalization and adversarial feature alignment to test-time adaptation and large-scale self-supervised pathology foundation models. Our analysis reveals a critical dichotomy between raw diagnostic performance and algorithmic equity: current optimization frameworks that successfully elevate aggregate macro metrics frequently do so by obscuring or actively exacerbating underlying demographic and subpopulation disparities. To achieve safe, equitable, and universally reliable clinical artificial intelligence, the field must transcend static validation habits. We outline a future roadmap anchored on three critical axes: establishing intersectional disparity indices as primary regulatory endpoints, standardizing multivendor metadata-rich benchmarks, and prioritizing.
topics: Artificial Intelligence in Healthcare and Education

documents.abstract: ABSTRACT This study examines how artificial intelligence (AI) capability can be mobilised as a strategic organisational capability for sustainable supply‐chain transformation. Integrating the Natural Resource‐Based View, Dynamic Capabilities Theory and Sociotechnical Systems Theory, the study argues that AI‐enabled sensing and decision support do not automatically translate into sustainability outcomes; strategic value emerges when technological resources, managerial competencies, human expertise and process routines are aligned. Green Lean Six Sigma (GLSS) is therefore conceptualised as an organisational architecture that converts AI‐generated insight into disciplined problem definition, waste and variation reduction, process redesign, standardisation and continuous improvement. Survey data from 361 managers and executives in supply‐chain‐intensive organisations across multiple Southeast Asian countries and sectors were analysed using partial least squares structural equation modelling. AI capability is positively associated with GLSS implementation, whereas GLSS is positively associated with environmental, economic and social supply‐chain performance. Significant indirect effects further show that GLSS acts as the transmission mechanism linking AI capability to all three triple‐bottom‐line outcomes. Because the estimated structural model did not include direct AI capability‐to‐performance paths, the evidence is interpreted as support for indirect effects rather than as proof of partial mediation. The study contributes to business strategy and sustainability research by explaining how an AI capability becomes strategically valuable when embedded in a sociotechnical improvement architecture. It also offers a staged managerial road map for harmonising AI investment, GLSS techniques and sustainable business transformation.

documents.abstract: ABSTRACT Urban gas systems are core components of global energy infrastructure, underpinning residential, commercial, and industrial energy supply while supporting low‐carbon goals. However, the growing frequency of urban gas accidents—from pipeline leaks to explosions—poses severe threats to energy security, public safety, and sustainable urban development, largely due to insufficient systematic analysis of root causes. This study addresses this gap by integrating accident causality theory, the 24‐Model, and the Human Factor Analysis and Classification System (HFACS) to investigate 100 urban gas accidents, combining Chinese (2014–2023) and global datasets. Using Apriori‐based Association Rule Mining (ARM), we identified 9 key risk factors, 19 critical association rules, and a universal causal chain, with institutional negligence (inadequate regulatory frameworks and weak supervision) confirmed as the predominant root cause. The key causal chain is: “lack of targeted energy safety regulations → poor supervision of gas infrastructure → unaddressed safety hazards → equipment failure in delivery systems → gas leakage (and subsequent ignition) → accident occurrence.” To mitigate these risks, we propose three actionable strategies: tailored safety regulations for urban gas networks, AI‐enhanced real‐time supervision systems, and competency‐based training programs. These insights not only optimize the resilience of China's gas energy systems but also provide a transferable framework for global urban energy safety management, aligning with goals for secure and sustainable urban energy.

This paper provides a scientific and methodological analysis of monitoring students' learning outcomes and assessing their individual development with artificial intelligence (AI) in a digital educational environment. It examines the content of learning outcome monitoring, the components on which it relies (data sources, indicators, analytical methods and feedback), and the opportunities offered by AI-based learning analytics. It also defines three groups of criteria for assessing individual development: the dynamics of results, the achievement of learning goals, and independent work and reflection. As a result, a six-stage methodology is proposed in which the teacher keeps the final pedagogical decision. The methodology is intended to support the timely and individualised assessment of students in higher education institutions.

Accurate and efficient point cloud registration is an important application of artificial intelligence for precise navigation and reliable decision-making in autonomous driving. However, the down-sampling of point clouds introduces interference from non-overlapping regions, resulting in the loss of important geometric information and a reduction in registration accuracy. Therefore, this study proposes an overlap-aware multi-level transformation regression network (OMTRNet), a deep-learning model that couples overlap prediction with frequency-domain and spatial feature interaction. Through a hierarchical feature extraction module designed with pixel grid mapping, we leverage the structural characteristics of pixel grids to efficiently extract point cloud features across multiple scales. By using a convolutional neural network-based overlap region prediction module, the overlap between the source and target point clouds at different scales is predicted. The overlapping region of the point cloud features is extracted from the predicted overlap, allowing for further feature extraction. Additionally, a frequency-domain feature interaction module is introduced to combine low-frequency global structural information with high-frequency local details as complementary cues for transformation estimation. Experimental results on the KITTI and NuScenes datasets validate the effectiveness of OMTRNet for large-scale partially overlapping point cloud registration. On the KITTI dataset, OMTRNet achieves an RTE of 0.2675 m, an RRE of 0.5342 deg, and a registration recall of 92.10%. The ablation results show that the DCT-based frequency-spatial interaction achieves competitive registration performance among the compared feature-interaction strategies.
topics: Advanced Image and Video Retrieval Techniques

documents.abstract: Abstract—Embodied Artificial Intelligence (AI) and autonomous robotic manipulation are undergoing an architectural paradigm shift from narrow, task-specific behavioral cloning policies toward generalist Multimodal Vision-Language-Action (VLA) foundation models. Pre-trained on Internet-scale vision-language corpora and fine-tuned across multi-robot demonstration datasets (e.g., Open X-Embodiment), VLA models—exemplified by RT-2, Octo, and OpenVLA—perceive high-resolution RGB-D sensor streams, process unstructured natural language instructions, and autoregressively predict or diffuse continuous 7-DoF robotic end-effector trajectories. However, translating disembodied multimodal foundation models into physical cyber-physical control fabrics introduces profound physical and computational bottlenecks: continuous action space tokenization discretization errors, severe cross-embodiment kinematic domain shifts across diverse robotic morphologies, closed-loop dynamic instability induced by non-deterministic neural inference latencies (>100 ms), and safety-critical execution failure modes. This paper presents an exhaustive, mathematically formal technical investigation and empirical benchmark of VLA models for robotic manipulation. We formalize the Markov Decision Process (MDP) bridging autoregressive tokenization with continuous trajectory diffusion policies, model cross-embodiment action normalization across disparate robotic arm kinematics, and derive Lyapunov-Krasovskii stability bounds under stochastic computational transport delays. Furthermore, we construct an empirical robotic evaluation testbed across physical Franka Emika Panda and simulated robotic workcells evaluating 600 complex manipulation trials spanning multi-stage semantic reasoning, spatial tool use, and long-horizon pick-and-place tasks. Our empirical findings demonstrate that continuous diffusion-policy action chunking achieves an 84.6% task success rate, outperforming discrete tokenization by 28.2% while reducing kinematic jerk by 62.4%. Concurrently, asynchronous visual-action decoupling bounds closed-loop inference latency within a deterministic 20 Hz control cycle. Finally, we formulate open research directions in tactile-integrated multi-modal perception, formal barrier certificates for physical safety, and self-supervised real-world policy refinement. Index Terms—Vision-Language-Action (VLA) Models, Embodied AI, Robotic Manipulation, Diffusion Policy, Action Tokenization, Cross-Embodiment Generalization, Open X-Embodiment, Closed-Loop Control Latency.

Ikisiri Utafiti huu ulilenga kuchunguza mchango wa emoji katika ujenzi na ufasiri wa maana za kipragmatiki katika diskosi za kidijitali za Kiswahili. Ingawa matumizi ya emoji yameongezeka katika mawasiliano ya mitandao ya kijamii, bado haijaelezwa kwa makini namna emoji zinavyoashiria msimamo wa mwasilishaji, kuimarisha kauli, kupunguza au kuongeza utata na kutekeleza matendo ya usemi kwa kuzingatia muktadha na dhamira ya mtumaji. Utafiti uliongozwa na Nadharia ya Umuhimu ya Sperber na Wilson (1995) na kutumia muundo wa kimaelezo. Data kuu zilijumuisha emoji 285 za aina 11 zilizokusanywa kimakusudi kutoka katika diskosi za Kiswahili kwenye WhatsApp na X. Aidha, washiriki 50 waliteuliwa kimakusudi ili kufasiri na kuthibitisha maana za emoji kulingana na muktadha. Data za ziada zilikusanywa kwa kutumia dodoso, mahojiano na majadiliano ya makundi lengwa. Emoji 285 zilitumika katika uchanganuzi mkuu, huku maoni ya washiriki yakisaidia ufasiri wake. Data zilichanganuliwa na kuwasilishwa kwa njia ya maelezo. Matokeo yalionyesha kuwa maana za emoji hujengwa kupitia mwingiliano wa vipengele vya kiisimu, kiutamaduni, kisemiotiki, kiteknolojia na kimwingiliano. Emoji zilibainika kuashiria mtazamo na dhamira ya mwasilishaji, kuimarisha au kurekebisha nguvu ya kauli, kutekeleza matendo ya usemi na kuelekeza ufasiri kulingana na muktadha. Utafiti huu unachangia uelewa wa emoji kama rasilimali za kipragmatiki na kutoa msingi wa tafiti zijazo kuhusu uchakataji wa lugha asilia kwa kutumia akili unde na maendeleo ya lugha za Kiafrika katika teknolojia ya kisasa. AbstractThis study examined the contribution of emojis to the construction and interpretation of pragmatic meaning in digital Kiswahili discourse. Although emoji use has increased in social media communication, insufficient attention has been given to how emojis signal the communicator’s stance, reinforce utterances, reduce or increase ambiguity, and perform speech acts in relation to context and the sender’s intention. The study was guided by Sperber and Wilson’s (1995) Relevance Theory and adopted a descriptive design. The main data comprised 285 emojis from 11 categories, purposively collected from Kiswahili discourse on WhatsApp and X. In addition, 50 participants were purposively selected to interpret and validate emoji meanings in context. Supplementary data were collected through questionnaires, interviews, and focus group discussions. The 285 emojis formed the primary data for analysis, while participants’ views supported their interpretation. Data were analysed and presented descriptively. The findings showed that emoji meanings are constructed through the interaction of linguistic, cultural, semiotic, technological, and interactional factors. Emojis were found to signal the communicator’s stance and intention, reinforce or modify the force of utterances, perform speech acts, and guide interpretation according to context. This study contributes to understanding emojis as pragmatic resources and provides a foundation for future research on natural language processing using artificial intelligence and the advancement of African languages in modern technology.

Abstract—Modern deep neural networks, particularly autoregressive Large Language Models (LLMs), have achieved state-of-the-art empirical performance across natural language generation, semantic translation, and broad pattern recognition. However, pure statistical connectionist architectures suffer from fundamental epistemological limitations: ungrounded factual hallucinations, an inability to guarantee mathematical soundness across multi-step deduction, brittle out-of-distribution reasoning, and a complete lack of formal explainability. Conversely, classical symbolic Artificial Intelligence (AI)—encompassing Satisfiability Modulo Theories (SMT) solvers, formal interactive theorem provers (e.g., Lean 4, Coq, Isabelle), and first-order ontological Knowledge Graphs—provides deterministic logical rigor, provable soundness, and certified safety verification, yet struggles with ambiguous perceptual inputs, continuous representations, and combinatorial state space explosion. Neuro-Symbolic AI establishes a transformative synthesis uniting statistical neural learning with rigorous symbolic reasoning. This paper presents an exhaustive, mathematically formal technical survey and empirical benchmark of neuro-symbolic systems across three mission-critical domains: automated mathematical olympiad proving, certified software verification, and high-stakes autonomous policy execution. We formalize differentiable fuzzy logic t-norm relaxations, model neural-guided proof search over formal tactic trees, and evaluate verified feedback loops using SMT counterexample-guided abstraction refinement (CEGAR). Furthermore, we construct an empirical evaluation testbed across 1,000 rigorous verification problems spanning the miniF2F formal mathematics benchmark, SMT-LIB program assertions, and complex multi-hop knowledge graphs. Our empirical findings demonstrate that neuro-symbolic integration elevates formal Lean 4 theorem proving success from 28.4% (pure LLM sampling) to 64.2% while guaranteeing 100% mathematical soundness. Concurrently, SMT-guided neural code repair eliminates 94.6% of verified runtime invariant violations. Finally, we formulate open challenges in end-to-end differentiable symbolic unification, scalable bidirectional semantic parsing, and certified neuro-symbolic alignment. Index Terms—Neuro-Symbolic AI, Automated Theorem Proving, Satisfiability Modulo Theories (SMT), Lean 4, Formal Verification, Knowledge Graphs, Differentiable Logic, Proof Search.

Dynamic warehouse task allocation must coordinate loading, transport and unloading robots under changing conditions. We propose a versioned neuro-symbolic architecture in which DeepSeek proposes facts and restricted rules, an authenticated semantic shield validates them, and a mivar-inspired knowledge layer supports deterministic allocation. Stage A selects bounded dispatch candidates using CP-SAT; Stage B performs conflict-aware route and unloading-service search. The service graph supports single-carrier, abstract coalition and same-origin batch transport. Frozen evaluation separates allocation (1800 simulation runs), grounding (6102 responses) and cached-DeepSeek effects (60 episodes). Equal-map-family semantic exactness was 99.52% for facts and 93.02% for rules, but only 69.53% for moving-congestion rules. Cached restricted rules met prespecified simulator-level non-inferiority criteria for deadline misses, distance and a distance-based energy proxy. An additional 150 exploratory episodes evaluate candidate size, early unloading-robot selection, semantic shielding and emulated asynchronous integration. A separately frozen test issued 1248 new API requests on 416 synthetic events. With the contemporaneous backend, revised prompting achieved 320/320 correct congestion transactions versus 317/320 with the original prompt, without significant template-level superiority (Holm-adjusted p = 0.50). Typed-field compilation also reached 320/320 but failed validation on 10/32 access-restriction events. Complete trusted structured inputs do not require an LLM. The contribution is an auditable, bounded semantic interface; physical-robot safety, live-network reliability and physical-energy benefits remain unvalidated.

Artificial intelligence is reshaping clinical medicine, requiring physicians to develop competencies that extend beyond traditional biomedical expertise into data literacy, algorithm interpretation, prompt design, and interdisciplinary collaboration with technical teams. As predictive models increasingly influence diagnosis, treatment planning, and healthcare system operations, clinicians must understand how algorithms are trained, validated, and deployed, as well as how to recognize bias, uncertainty, and performance limitations. This chapter outlines a progressive framework of expertise ranging from basic clinical users of AI tools to clinician-scientists and clinician-engineers who co-design and evaluate intelligent health systems. It examines how digital professionalism, ethical stewardship, regulatory awareness, and patient communication must evolve in parallel with technical capability. Ultimately, the digital doctor is not defined by programming proficiency but by the ability to interpret machine-generated insight responsibly and integrate it with human judgment to ensure that artificial intelligence strengthens equitable, safe, and patient-centered care.

documents.abstract: Organizations are adopting generative AI and AI decision support in professional work while evidence on their effects is still accumulating. Empirical studies document substantial productivity gains in some settings and losses in others, and practitioners carry assumptions formed during early use into everyday professional work. Research on the resulting problems is spread across human factors, human-computer interaction, fairness research, empirical economics and law, and no consolidated framework for professional use was found. This paper proposes such a framework. Its format is inspired by the Fallacies of Distributed Computing, a short list of false assumptions well known in software engineering; its content is specific to professional AI usage. Through an integrative review of peer-reviewed studies, randomized and preregistered trials, court decisions, provider documentation and regulation, nine fallacies are derived: (1) the output is correct; (2) capability is uniform across tasks; (3) the human reviewer is a reliable safeguard; (4) perceived productivity equals actual productivity; (5) AI removes work; (6) accountability moves to the tool or vendor; (7) skills and system understanding stay intact when work is delegated; (8) results transfer from benchmarks and pilots; and (9) the model is available. For each fallacy, the paper explains why the assumption persists, presents the evidence against it, states the conditions under which it does hold, and grades the strength of the evidence. It then analyzes how fallacies can compound, with particular attention to agent-built software systems that may become difficult to maintain when AI access is lost. The paper closes with implications for practice, a research agenda and a self-assessment instrument.

documents.abstract: The accuracy of machine learning interatomic potentials suffers from reference data that contain numerical noise. Often originating from unconverged or inconsistent electronic-structure calculations, this noise is challenging to identify. Existing mitigation strategies, such as manual filtering or iterative refinement of outliers, require either substantial expert effort or multiple expensive retraining cycles, making them difficult to scale to large datasets. Here, we introduce a noise-resilient training method that automatically down-weighs noisy samples, without requiring additional reference calculations. By tracking the loss distribution via an exponential moving average, this unsupervised method identifies outliers throughout a single training run. We show that this approach prevents overfitting and matches the performance of iterative refinement baselines with significantly reduced overhead. The method’s effectiveness is demonstrated by recovering accurate physical observables for liquid water from unconverged reference data, including diffusion coefficients. Furthermore, we validate its scalability by training a foundation model for organic chemistry on the SPICE dataset, where it reduces both energy and force errors. This framework provides a simple, automated solution for training robust models on imperfect datasets across dataset sizes.

Medical students occupy an unusual position in the hospital: they are learners, yet they work in the same wards, theatres, and emergency rooms as fully trained staff, often with the least experience, the least authority, and the fewest protective habits. This narrative article reviews the occupational health hazards they face during clinical training and argues that these hazards are neither rare nor incidental, but structural. The hazards are organized into five families — biological (needlestick injuries and blood borne pathogens such as HIV, hepatitis B and C, and tuberculosis), chemical (antineoplastic drugs, anaesthetic gases, disinfectants), physical (radiation, noise, slips and falls), ergonomic (patient handling, long standing hours), and psychological (sleep deprivation, burnout, depression, and bullying) — each illustrated with examples and, where possible, figures from the published literature. Tables summarize the hazard categories and the reasons students are disproportionately exposed. The article concludes that protecting students requires more than personal protective equipment: it demands vaccination, safety-engineered devices, enforced reporting systems, duty hour limits, and above all a clinical culture in which asking for help is a sign of professionalism rather than weakness.
topics: Occupational Health and Safety in Workplaces

documents.abstract: This paper presents a structured narrative review of ten empirical studies published between 2008 and 2025, examining the relationships between heat exposure, hydration and kidney-related outcomes among construction workers. The studies were identified through targeted searches of Scopus and PubMed and interpreted using an ergonomics-informed work systems perspective. The findings suggest that construction workers are frequently exposed to heat levels that exceed recommended safety thresholds, with dehydration remaining common under real-world site conditions. Across the studies, there are indications of recurring kidney stress, including biomarkers associated with acute kidney injury (AKI), although reported rates vary due to differences in study design and measurement methods. Evidence relating to longer-term outcomes is still limited and remains inconclusive. A key contribution of this study is the development of a conceptual framework that brings together environmental heat exposure, pathophysiological response pathways and organisational and behavioural influences within a work systems context. This framework suggests that heat-related kidney risk is influenced not only by environmental exposure, but also by the interaction between work demands, organisational conditions and the factors that shape worker behaviours. Evidence points towards the need for multi-level strategies to protect workers, including better hydration practices, more adaptive work–rest scheduling and improved occupational health monitoring. The review also highlights important gaps in current knowledge, particularly the need for more longitudinal research and greater consistency in how outcomes are measured. Addressing heat-related kidney risks will be increasingly important for protecting worker health and supporting safe and sustainable construction practices in a warming climate.
topics: Occupational Health and Safety in Workplaces

documents.abstract: In archaeological scholarship, the challenge of interpreting large amounts of fragmented evidence can be daunting. This paper will examine how artificial intelligence can assist in this process, mainly through examining visual evidence and classifying material evidence. Drawing from Trevor Paglen's argument of machine vision and Matteo Pasquinelli's history of classification in machines, this paper develops an analysis of two archaeological case studies: archaeological site detection based on satellite imagery in Mesopotamia and deep-learning classification of Tusayan White Ware pottery. The findings of the studies demonstrate that artificial intelligence is capable of expanding preliminary surveys as well as applying typologies consistently. At the same time, they also highlight the importance of human input, coming to the conclusion that artificial intelligence's potential and principal contribution lies in simplifying the archaeological process and directing human attention towards evidence requiring further interpretation, establishing a framework for understanding artificial intelligence as an assistive technology.

Combined with machine learning techniques, ontologies have recently been applied widely to enhance decision-making, reasoning, knowledge management and representation, and information retrieval in various domains. Likewise, the popularity of ontologies is increasing in the rapidly evolving field of precision agriculture due to the ability to encode general domain knowledge and specialized knowledge of farmers and utilize it within data processing and analytics pipelines. Although the research on ontologies applied to precision agriculture problems is increasing, adopting published solutions is rather cumbersome, mainly due to low reproducibility of these works. This article is intended to survey the current applied research in ontologies within the agricultural domain, by investigating the used methodologies, technologies and evaluation approaches, the availability of the data, ontologies and source codes developed. It was found that the used data sources, the developed ontologies and the developed source codes are available only in 14%, 9% and 7%, respectively, of the selected 85 articles. Additionally, it was found that the applied methodologies, in relation to the issue of reproducibility, the top-down/bottom-up, semi-automatic, seven-step and ontology matching approaches have shown greater potential, while according to the applied technologies, World Wide Web (W3C) have shown greater contribution compared to artificial intelligence (AI).

In isolated, confined and extreme (ICE) environments, prolonged sensory monotony, limited space and sustained task demands may affect operators’ cognitive performance and workload state, with potential consequences for mission safety and system reliability. This small-sample exploratory longitudinal repeated-measures study involved seven male participants in a 30-day simulated ICE mission and examined operator responses to a virtual reality (VR) cognitive and motor task at the pre-isolation and post-isolation measurement windows. The experimental factors were the pre-isolation and post-isolation measurement windows and the pre-VR and post-VR task phases. At each window, participants completed Stroop, Vigilance and reversed digit memory tasks, while cognitive task performance, subjective scales, VR movement behavior, electroencephalography (EEG) and functional near-infrared spectroscopy (fNIRS) signals were recorded. After Benjamini–Hochberg false discovery rate (BH-FDR) correction, the clearest changes occurred in the Stroop task. Compared with the pre-isolation measurement window, the post-isolation window showed a higher Stroop completion count, a lower average reaction time and lower EEG Delta-band wavelet amplitude in the left occipital lobe, right occipital lobe, left motor cortex and left prefrontal cortex. In the pre-VR versus post-VR comparison, Stroop completion count increased and average reaction time decreased after VR. Other results from EEG effective connectivity, fNIRS, subjective scales, VR behavior and cross-modal associations did not show similarly stable corrected differences. The findings indicate that cognitive performance and neurophysiological measures describe different aspects of operator-state changes during confined, high-demand operations and may inform operator workload assessment, multimodal state monitoring and VR task design in ICE and similar operational environments.

Abstract—The relentless exponential scaling of foundation models and transformer architectures has pushed conventional silicon complementary metal-oxide-semiconductor (CMOS) digital accelerators (GPUs, TPUs) toward fundamental thermodynamic and interconnect boundaries. Joule heating, resistance-capacitance (RC) interconnect delay scaling, and the 'memory wall' severely constrain energy efficiency and compute density. Optical Computing and Integrated Silicon Photonics (SiPh) establish an analog non-Von Neumann hardware paradigm that executes fundamental linear algebra operations—specifically General Matrix-Matrix Multiplication (GEMM)—at the speed of light with near-zero runtime energy dissipation. By encoding vector-matrix activations into coherent optical wave fields and modulating light through cascaded Mach-Zehnder Interferometer (MZI) meshes, Micro-Ring Resonator (MRR) banks, and Wavelength-Division Multiplexing (WDM) waveguides, photonic tensor processing units (PTPUs) execute analog matrix multiplications in continuous time with sub-nanosecond propagation latencies. However, translating integrated photonic circuits into production deep learning accelerators introduces profound optoelectronic engineering bottlenecks: analog noise accumulation across deep optical meshes, severe thermal phase drift, limited electro-optic Digital-to-Analog / Analog-to-Digital (DAC/ADC) conversion resolution, non-linear activation implementation hurdles, and wafer-scale optical footprint scaling. This paper delivers an exhaustive, mathematically formal technical investigation and empirical benchmark of integrated photonic computing for deep neural network acceleration. We formalize the Clements and Reck unitary matrix decomposition algorithms over reconfigurable MZI topologies, derive the optical transmission transfer matrix under optical carrier phase error perturbations, and establish energy-per-MAC physical thermodynamic bounds across electro-optic conversion interfaces. Furthermore, we construct an empirical co-simulation and hardware testbed benchmarking silicon photonic meshes against state-of-the-art CMOS accelerators (NVIDIA H100, Google TPU v5p) across vision transformers, large language model attention heads, and resonant graph convolutions. Our empirical findings demonstrate that a 64x64 integrated MZI photonic mesh achieves a 58.4x improvement in energy-delay product (EDP) over 4nm digital CMOS cores, sustaining up to 128 Tera-Operations per Second per Watt (TOPS/W) at 4-bit to 8-bit equivalent precision, while active thermo-optic phase stabilization preserves 98.2% baseline classification accuracy. Finally, we establish open research directions in all-optical non-linear activation functions, co-packaged optical memory architectures, and wafer-scale photonic interconnect scaling. Index Terms—Photonic Computing, Silicon Photonics (SiPh), Mach-Zehnder Interferometer (MZI), Wavelength-Division Multiplexing (WDM), Optical Neural Networks (ONNs), Matrix-Vector Multiplication, Energy-Efficient Accelerators.

Crime-related social media content provides valuable information for situational awareness and policy support; however, engagement-driven signals, such as likes and retweets, can introduce popularity bias and affect predictive outcomes. This study proposes a fairness-aware, Pareto-based, multi-objective optimization framework for feature selection and Random Forest hyperparameter optimization, leveraging textual and engagement features. A dataset of 32,000 crime-related tweets covering Fraud, Accident, and Murder was represented using TF-IDF and interaction-based features. Four optimization strategies, Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO), Ant Colony Optimization (ACO), Evolutionary Reinforcement Learning (ERL), and Non-Dominated Sorting Genetic Algorithm II (NSGA-II), were comparatively evaluated. NSGA-II jointly maximized classification performance while minimizing a fairness penalty based on Statistical Parity Difference (SPD), Disparate Impact (DI), and Equality of Opportunity Difference (EOD). In this study, fairness refers to mitigating engagement-driven popularity bias across behavioral user groups rather than demographic discrimination. NSGA-II achieved an accuracy of 0.8118 and an F1-score of 0.8051, with an SPD of 0.08, DI of 0.97, and EOD of 0.06, demonstrating the most favorable balance between predictive performance and behavioral fairness. Although removing engagement features improved standalone Accuracy and F1-score, retaining them enabled explicit assessment and mitigation of engagement-driven bias. Stratified cross-validation and comparative analysis across the optimization strategies further supported the consistency of the observed results. The findings demonstrate that integrating fairness objectives directly into Pareto-based optimization provides a practical and interpretable approach to balancing predictive effectiveness and engagement-driven fairness in crime-related social media analytics.
